title: Cobalt Therapeutics - Private Deployment Egress & KMS Deep Dive
summary: Deep dive on private/VPC deployment security: ingress/egress controls, egress whitelisting, KMS integration (BYOK/HSM), audit log flows to SIEM, and SOC2 implications. Agreed to run a limited pilot in a staging VPC and provide an architecture diagram + egress rule spreadsheet.
topics: VPC egress controls and whitelist strategy
Audit log forwarding and retention for SOC2
On-prem/offline package constraints and image registry
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-04 15:30 UTC | Duration 55m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Rahul Singh (Redwood SE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood Product Sec), Aisha Rahman (Cobalt CISO), Tom Lin (Infra), Priya Mehta (SecOps), Markus Vogel (DevOps)

Summary section (auto): short recap at end.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, we got Aisha, Tom, Priya, Markus on the customer side?
[00:06] Aisha: Yep, that's us. Thanks for arranging. We mostly want to validate an architecture for a private deployment — strict egress, KMS BYOK, and how logs get to our SIEM without leaving the VPC.
[00:15] Rahul: Great, we'll walk through the control plane model, how our private package works, and options for key management. Diego will chime in on audit/audit logs and SOC 2 considerations.
[00:22] Markus: Quick ask — we run a locked-down staging environment first. No outbound DNS except a few hosts, and no internet egress from production. Is that supported?
[00:30] Rahul: Yes, we support private control plane with a customer-managed VPC. Two common patterns: 1) fully air-gapped on-prem bundle; 2) VPC-enabled private deployment where all egress is via NAT or egress proxy and we can restrict to specific IP ranges or DNS names.
[00:44] Tom: How do you handle model downloads/updates? We require checksum verification and prefer pulling from our private ECR or an internal artifact repo.
[00:51] Diego: We can configure artifact pulling to use your registry — the private package supports config for registry URL and image pull secrets. We also verify signatures if you enable image signing. There's a small bootstrap that may need a once-off outbound call for license verification; if you want zero egress, we have an offline bundle process.
[01:08] Priya: Offline bundle sounds interesting. Does that include precompiled kernels? We can't let nodes reach out to any S3 endpoints in prod.
[01:14] Rahul: Offline bundle includes model artifacts, runtime binaries, and a manifest. You can ingest it via internal tooling. For updates, you can stage via a secured S3 with VPC endpoint or an internal artifact proxy.
[01:23] Aisha: Okay. Let's talk KMS. We require BYOK with HSM-backed keys and key rotation under our control. What's the integration story?
[01:31] Diego: Two options: customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS with multi-account grants or Azure Key Vault) where Redwood is a principal that can request decrypt via grants; or customer-hosted HSM that performs decrypts locally. For BYOK, we support envelope encryption — Redwood service stores only wrapped keys. Key wrapping uses your KMS to unwrap at runtime.
[01:49] Markus: So the unwrapping happens inside our VPC only? We need to ensure plaintext keys never leave our HSM boundary.
[01:56] Rahul: Correct. For the HSM path the decryption happens on your side and we never see the plaintext. For the AWS KMS flow, the KMS decrypt/generate-data-key operation is invoked by components running in your VPC — so plaintext keys are only in-memory within your VPC processes. We support KMS grants and IAM roles scoped to the instance profile.
[02:13] Tom: What about HSM connectors for on-prem Thales/NetHSM?
[02:17] Diego: We have integrations via PKCS#11 and can call to an HSM over the appropriate secure channel. If you want, our engineers can do a short compatibility test.
[02:25] Aisha: Audit logs — we need immutable logs with 365+ days retention for SOC 2 readiness and the ability to stream to Splunk. How do you expose audit trails?
[02:34] Diego: We emit audit events for user actions, model invocations, admin changes, and key events. For private deployments we can stream those to your SIEM via a VPC endpoint: either Kinesis/Firehose or directly to a syslog collector via fluentd/Vector. We also support S3 + VPC endpoint with server-side encryption — we can sign and append a manifest to maintain chain of custody.
[02:56] Priya: Are flow logs packaged too? We want VPC Flow Logs and AWS Network Firewall logs correlated.
[03:01] Rahul: Yes, recommended: enable VPC Flow Logs, AWS Network Firewall, and we can push our service logs to the same account or cross-account role. We also support exporting to your central logging account via a cross-account Kinesis or S3 replication.
[03:14] Markus: Egress controls — we use explicit deny with security groups and NACLs. How granular can Redwood be? FQDN, IP, or TLS SNI?
[03:24] Rahul: Internally, our side relies on IP/CIDR for low-level filtering, but we do support egress proxies for FQDN-level allow lists. Two deployment choices: 1) enforce IP/CIDR allowlist at the outbound gateway (NAT or proxy) and allow only your registry and telemetry endpoints; 2) use an Envoy/sidecar that enforces FQDN and SNI inspection inside the cluster. We don't recommend deep TLS interception because that breaks cert pinning — better to use mTLS and allow specific hostnames.
[03:49] Tom: We need to prevent model telemetry from ever going to Redwood-hosted endpoints — telemetry must go to an internal collector. Is it possible to route all telemetry to our account?
[03:58] Diego: Yes, telemetry endpoints can be configured to point to your internal collector. We can provide an option for no-call-home; in that mode error reporting and metrics are forwarded to your endpoints only. For supported features where Redwood-hosted control plane is disabled, some managed features like automatic model updates will be opt-in.
[04:17] Aisha: How does this tie into SOC 2? We need control evidence for encryption in transit & at rest, access logs, and RBAC policies.
[04:24] Diego: For SOC 2, we'd provide documentation of encryption (TLS 1.2/1.3), audit event schemas, and evidence of RBAC and SSO integration. We also recommend SCIM provisioning so user lifecycle is auditable. Our audit logs include user IDs and request IDs to correlate with model calls.
[04:37] Priya: On RBAC: can we integrate with Okta and map AD groups to roles? We want least-privilege role mapping (viewer, operator, admin, auditor).
[04:45] Rahul: Yes, we support SAML SSO with Okta and SCIM for provisioning. Role mapping can be done via group assertions; we expose built-in roles that you can customize. We also log role changes as admin events.
[04:57] Markus: A quick nit: does your private control plane expose any public endpoints for healthchecks or license validation?
[05:03] Rahul: Only if you enable them. Default is no public endpoints; health checks can be routed to an internal ALB/NLB. License validation can be done offline; otherwise it uses a short-lived outbound to a Redwood endpoint.
[05:15] Tom: For egress we want explicit allowlist to a handful of CIDR blocks and to our internal KMS. Do you support egress via interface VPC endpoints?
[05:22] Diego: Absolutely — VPC interface endpoints for S3, KMS, and ECR are supported. That keeps traffic on the AWS network and avoids internet egress.
[05:30] Aisha: Regarding data residency: certain model usage logs must stay in-region EU. Can you pin storage region?
[05:36] Rahul: If you run the private deployment in an EU region for the nodes and storage, all persistent logs and payloads remain in-region. For cross-region backups we can disable replication or use customer-managed encryption that restricts access.
[05:47] Priya: We have a question on operator privileges: our platform team needs to debug latency issues but we can't allow token export. Is there a safe debug mode?
[05:55] Diego: We provide an operator debugging role that yields trace-level logs but redacts secrets and full prompt text unless explicitly unredacted with a two-person approval flow. We can also provide ephemeral session recording with justification metadata for audits.
[06:11] Maya: (interrupting) There was a question earlier about firewalling between model-serving pods and internal data stores?
[06:16] Tom: Yes — we want network segmentation between inference nodes and our PHI stores.
[06:20] Rahul: We recommend separate subnets and security groups. Use NACLs for subnet-level protection and security groups for service-level ingress. For extra isolation, place inference nodes in a private subnet with no route to the data subnet and use a dedicated proxy that implements fine-grained queries with parameterized endpoints.
[06:35] Markus: Any recommendations on eBPF or service mesh?
[06:38] Diego: eBPF can give visibility but requires kernel modules; for most customers Envoy sidecar + mTLS suffices. If you need kernel-level filtering we can discuss a hardened host image where eBPF probes are pre-approved.
[06:50] Aisha: Competitors have pushed the idea of 'zero egress' by bundling everything; how does Redwood differ operationally?
[06:57] Maya: We support both. The difference is our managed offering gives automated rollouts and observability; the private/offline bundle gives you zero egress but trades off automation. We'll help you pick the right tradeoffs per environment.
[07:08] Priya: Anything about compliance reporting for ISO 27001?
[07:11] Diego: Very similar to SOC 2; we provide evidence packages, risk assessments for our private deployment, and third-party pen test reports if you need them. For ISO you'd map our controls to your ISMS.
[07:22] Tom: For the pilot, we want a strict egress spreadsheet listing every destination and port. Can you produce one?
[07:28] Rahul: Yes — we'll attach an egress whitelist template. It includes CIDR, FQDN, port, purpose, and recommended alternative (VPC endpoint etc).
[07:37] Aisha: Also, can you provide a short runbook for seizure scenarios — if keys are compromised, rotate and revoke?
[07:43] Diego: We'll provide a key-rotation playbook: revoke grants, rotate KMS keys, rewrap artifacts, and forensic steps.
[07:50] Markus: For the compatibility test, who owns the test harness?
[07:53] Maya: Redwood will provide a small test harness repo; we'll need an engineer from your side to run it in staging.
[07:59] Tom: Timeline? We want to be SOC 2 ready by Q3. A pilot in staging in 4 weeks would be ideal.
[08:05] Rahul: That sounds doable. We'll deliver the architecture diagram, egress spreadsheet, and the BYOK compatibility checklist in the next week.
[08:13] Aisha: Any blockers for us to run an on-prem offline bundle for an initial proof?
[08:17] Diego: Only a signature verification step and ensuring your image registry accepts the signed artifacts. We'll include step-by-step packaging instructions.
[08:26] Maya: Great. I'll summarize next steps at the end. Any final quick questions?
[08:31] Priya: One small thing — do you keep command-level audit of admin console actions?
[08:35] Diego: Yes, admin console actions are audited with userid, timestamp, request id, and we can forward those to your SIEM.
[08:42] Markus: Good.
[08:44] Maya: Okay we'll wrap up. Thanks everyone.
